headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Upgrading Your Bathroom Vanity Cabinet
articleBody:
Planning a vanity upgrade requires attention to subtle structural details. Here are common mistakes property owners encounter and how to avoid them:

1. Skipping the rough plumbing check: Buying a vanity before measuring existing water lines and drain pipe heights often leads to shelves or drawers colliding with pipes. Always verify interior clearance before purchasing.
2. Reusing damaged shutoff valves: Keeping old, crusty shutoff valves or worn tubular traps invites slow leaks. Replace valves and aged drain assemblies while plumbing is accessible.
3. Forgetting door and drawer clearances: Installing a vanity too close to door casings, toilets, or shower enclosures can block drawers from fully extending. Map out full swing paths beforehand.
4. Installing on an uneven floor without shims: Cabinets set directly on uneven tile without proper leveling put uneven stress on countertop slabs. Always level the base in both directions.
5. Neglecting wall anchoring: Relying on drywall anchors instead of driving structural screws into wall studs can cause cabinets to pull away under the weight of a stone top.
6. Skipping thorough leak testing: Turning on the water for ten seconds is not enough. Fill the basin, pull the stopper, and inspect every joint under drain pressure.
